path_policy.path_expansion: Expand <temporary-root> once to a fresh absolute root; each argv template uses the declared per-template working directory.

path_encoding.canonical_form: absolute path with forward slashes in the copied Java-properties value
path_encoding.windows_form: A future runner may use backslashes only when each backslash is Java-properties escaped as \\; shell quoting is not path escaping.

actions: Load and dirty the plan in the GUI.
Invoke the GUI Start action with save_automatically_before_run=true and no save_before_run preference.
Record the save-before-run event, backup event, and resulting recent_file_0.
preference_scenarios.expected: property fallback enables autosave before run

actions: Seed save_before_run=true, then load and dirty the plan in the GUI.
Record that the existing true preference wins and capture save/backup order.
Seed save_before_run=false, then load and dirty the plan in the GUI.
Record that no autosave or backup occurs before the run despite the true property fallback.
Do not load a plan through the GUI and invoke the -n -t LAST -l LAST -j LAST template from the declared last-command working directory.
Record the explicit missing recent_file_0 diagnostic and do not guess a plan from the fixture or current directory.
preference_scenarios.expected: unavailable/error; no ambient preference or guessed path

required: Set java.util.prefs.userRoot before JVM startup; LAST and save-before-run otherwise read ambient state.
Do not pass the literal ${JMETER_HOME} string to JMeter and expect interpolation.
The GUI save-as path is <temporary-root>/oracle-runs/gui-static/persistence-contracts/last/saved-plan.jmx; the following LAST commands use its recent_file_0 entry.

bounds.enforcement: declared; static-only; future runner must enforce

future_oracle_actions: Materialize the referenced original plan and gui-persistence.properties at the declared workspace destinations, and allocate a fresh preference root and output directory for each preference_scenarios entry; do not write generated files under this corpus.

Launch the GUI, mark the plan dirty, save repeatedly, and record the backup directory, first six-digit name (000001), sequence, maximum count, and maximum-age behavior. Backups are created only for an existing file and a dirty save.

Run fallback_absent, preference_true, and preference_false with their fresh cleared roots and exact GUI Start action. Record whether autosave occurs, the save/backup event order, and which preference/property value supplied the decision.

For a positive LAST run, save-as to <temporary-root>/oracle-runs/gui-static/persistence-contracts/last/saved-plan.jmx so recent_file_0 is absolute and isolated, then run both LAST argv templates from the declared last-command working directory. -l LAST derives saved-plan.jtl; -j LAST remains the literal LAST log path in that working directory. Run last_missing_recent separately and require an explicit unavailable/error diagnostic.

Resolve template.files as JMeterHome + /bin/templates/templates.xml, record template names/descriptions and selected output, and verify the empty WorkBench is discarded while the non-empty migration case produces a disabled TestFragmentController.
limitations: The property file and filesystem layout are original descriptors; no backup, autosave, LAST, template, or WorkBench event was observed.
The command templates are future oracle inputs, not commands run during corpus creation.
Path normalization is limited to the temporary root token declared in the expected descriptor; directory contents and numbering remain evidence fields.
The literal ${JMETER_HOME} token is never treated as JMeter expansion; only the future runner may replace it in an isolated property-file copy.
The Java preferences root is a future-run isolation requirement; no LAST resolution, save event, process exit, or diagnostic was observed.
